Whenever a creature attempts to move through a space adjacent to them, that creature must save vs. Blast to avoid being scratched; the referee should make these saving throws in secret the first time a creature passes by a rosebush. Attempting to touch a rosebush, even on an apparently non-thorny part of a vine, is treated as failing this saving throw.

A creature that fails this saving throw immediately suffers 1d6+1 piercing damage and ongoing bleeding damage, as the vines twist and lash to drive the thorns deeper into their flesh. If this damage die rolls a '6', that creature is grabbed and restrained by the thornbushes unless they succeed at a save vs. Hold, suffering another d6 piercing damage as they are grabbed. A restrained creature suffers another d6 piercing damage each round, and must use their action to make a hard save vs. Hold until they manage to free themselves.

As the bloodroses inflict damage, the flowers around them change color from white, to pink, to deep red. Whenever a creature critically fails their saving throw vs. a bush, that creature suffers a critical hit and all the petals fall off of the blooms on that 5' patch of bush. The next round, each of the exposed rose hips explode, sending razor-sharp shrapnel in a blast 4 paces in radius that deals 3d6+1 piercing damage and ongoing bleeding damage. The next round after that, every inch of exposed surface within the blast area starts growing new rosevines, which continue to grow and mature over 1d6 rounds until they produce their own thorns and flowers.

Each 5' patch of bloodrose is treated as a separate large "creature" with 1d6 structure points, although they have no abilities and cannot move or perform actions. Attack throws against a bloodrose are easy, since it fills a 5' space and can't move or dodge.

Attacks from an ax weapon or fire inflict direct structure damage, while other attacks follow the normal rules for attacking a structure. If a bloodrose is lit on fire, it has a 1- in-6 chance of spreading the flames to each adjacent bush.

This same energy makes the plants vulnerable to the rebuke the unholy miracle, which inflicts 1d6 structure damage to each plant within 10 paces, and prevents those plants from regenerating when further damage is inflicted on them.
